title: jpack.json project configuration
description: A NON-NORMATIVE convention of the judgment-pack runtime (ADR-0012), not part of the Judgment Pack Specification. It names the packs a project owns and where they live, relative to this file's own directory. It selects nothing at decision time, templates nothing, and holds no pack's version as a truth of its own: a pack's identity is the pack document's, and every reference to it here is validated against that document rather than believed.

configVersion.description: The version of this configuration format. A single integer as a string, on the outputVersion precedent rather than semantic versioning; "1" is the only value this runtime accepts, and this schema accepts no other, so a configuration held to these exact bytes is held to what the runtime will actually read. A later shape will be "2", published with the runtime that reads it.

packs.description: The project's packs, keyed by decision id. The key is the project's own name for one decision; the pack document's id member is the pack's identity and is not this key. At least one pack is required: a configuration declaring none describes no project, and accepting it would let a test run report a clean result over zero rows. The runner demotes a zero-row run to "skipped" regardless, so this constraint is the earlier of two independent refusals rather than the only one.

relativePath.description: A path relative to this configuration file's own directory, which it must resolve inside. Two different checks say so and neither substitutes for the other: a lexical check refuses an absolute or escaping path before anything is read, and at read time the path is resolved against a handle held open on that directory -- which is what catches a path reaching outside through a symlinked component, since a lexical check cannot see one, and what keeps containment true through the open rather than only up to it. A final component that is a symlink is refused whatever it points at, and only a regular file is read.

path.description: The pack document, relative to this file's directory.

matrix.description: The pack's instance matrix, relative to this file's directory. Rows use the same case-carrier shape as the bundled evaluation corpus.

description.description: One line about the decision this pack encodes, for a human or an agent reading the inventory.

expectedVersion.description: The pack document version this project expects. It is a validated reference and never an independent truth: packs validate reports a difference from the document's own version member as an error rather than preferring either value.

facts.description: NON-NORMATIVE agent hints, keyed by the RFC 6901 JSON Pointer the pack's conditions read. They say where a fact is found; they are not facts, and this runtime never reads a source. The key is checked against the pack document by packs validate: a pointer no condition reads is reported as a failed check rather than handed to an agent as an instruction.

evidence.description: NON-NORMATIVE agent hints, keyed by the pack's declared evidence-requirement ids. They say where evidence is found; they are not evidence, and this runtime never reads a source. The key is checked against the pack document by packs validate: an id the pack declares no requirement for is reported as a failed check.

source.description: Where the value is authoritatively held, in the project's own words -- a warehouse table, a document library, a service. The runtime holds no credential and opens no connection; reading it is the agent's job, with the agent's own access.

hint.description: How to obtain the value from that source, in the project's own words.
